channel.title: DevTools Online Blog
channel.description: Tutorials, guides, and deep dives on JSON, SQL, JWT, encoding, security, and the developer tools we build.

item.title: WCAG Color Contrast: Passing AA, AAA, and What Designers Get Wrong
item.description: Light grey on white is the most common accessibility failure. Twenty percent of users can't read it. The fix is a 30-second check, but you have to know what to check for.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: UUID v4 vs v7: Why You Probably Want v7 in New Code
item.description: UUID v4 dominated for 15 years because it was 'good enough.' UUID v7 fixes the one real problem v4 had, random UUIDs are terrible primary keys. The migration is overdue.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: User-Agent Strings Are a Mess: Parsing Them Without Pulling Your Hair Out
item.description: The User-Agent string is a 30-year-old archaeology site. Every browser still claims to be Mozilla 5.0. Chrome claims to be Safari. The reasons are historical and the parsing is a tax we still pay.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: URL Encoding Cheatsheet: %20 vs +, Percent-Encoding, Common Pitfalls
item.description: URL encoding looks like one rule until you realize space is %20 in paths and + in query strings, and there are four different JavaScript functions and they all do slightly different things.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: TOTP and 2FA: How 6-Digit Codes That Refresh Every 30 Seconds Work
item.description: TOTP looks like magic, six digits that match between your phone and the server, refreshing every 30 seconds. The actual algorithm fits in 20 lines of code, and the failure modes are surprisingly mundane.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: SSL/TLS Certificate Chains: Why Your Cert Works in Chrome but Fails in curl
item.description: Browsers fix incomplete certificate chains for you. curl, Java, Python, and most server-to-server tools don't. Half the 'TLS works in browser but fails everywhere else' bugs trace back to a missing intermediate cert.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: SQL Formatting: From Unreadable Queries to Pull-Request-Ready Code
item.description: Most SQL is unreadable because nobody formats it. Run it through a formatter once, agree on a style, and your team's queries become reviewable code instead of write-only blobs.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Generating Secure Passwords: Entropy, Length, and the Math That Matters
item.description: Your password isn't secure because it's long. It's secure because it's unguessable. The math that connects 'unguessable' to 'how many characters' is simpler than you'd think.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Regex in 2026: When to Use It, When You Should Have Used a Parser
item.description: If you've ever spent two days debugging a regex that 'worked on the test cases,' this post is for you. Regex has a sweet spot. Outside it, every problem is harder than the regex you're tempted to write.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: QR Codes for Developers: Error Correction, SVG vs PNG, and the Math Inside
item.description: QR codes are everywhere, and most teams generate them with no thought. The defaults are usually fine. The 5% of cases where you need to think, printed labels, branded codes, dynamic redirects, is where this post earns its keep.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Prettier vs ESLint: Stop Confusing Formatting with Linting
item.description: Prettier and ESLint do different jobs. Half the JavaScript ecosystem treats them as alternatives. The other half configures both badly and they fight. Here's how to wire them up so they don't.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Mermaid Diagrams in Documentation: Beyond ASCII Art
item.description: ASCII art belongs in 1995. Mermaid diagrams are real diagrams, written as text, rendered automatically by GitHub, GitLab, Notion, and every modern docs platform. Here's the practical guide.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: MD5 Is Dead. SHA-256, SHA-512, BCrypt. Picking the Right Hash for the Job
item.description: MD5 still has uses in 2026. Hashing passwords isn't one of them. Pick the algorithm based on what you're protecting against, collisions, brute force, or just integrity.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: JWT Decoded: How Tokens Work and Why Invalid Signature Happens
item.description: A JWT is three Base64URL strings separated by dots. The first two are JSON. The third is a signature. About half the JWT bugs in production come from people forgetting that last detail.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Validating JSON in 2026: JSON Schema, AJV, and the Browser-Native Approach
item.description: Compile-time TypeScript types catch the typos. Runtime validators catch what the API actually sent. The trick is knowing which validator to reach for, and when validation belongs at the boundary.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: JSON to TypeScript: Generating Type-Safe Interfaces from API Responses
item.description: Hand-typing TypeScript interfaces from a 4KB API payload is the work of a punished engineer. There are three good ways to skip that, pick the one that fits your trust level for the upstream API.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Why Your JSON Has a BOM (Byte Order Mark) and How to Strip It
item.description: Your JSON parser fails at character 0 and the error message tells you nothing. Nine times out of ten, it's a UTF-8 BOM that some Windows tool added when you weren't looking.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: HTTP Status Codes: The Ones You Actually Need to Know in 2026
item.description: There are 60+ HTTP status codes. About 25 matter. About 10 are the difference between a clear API and a confusing one. Here's the practical map.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: HTML Entity Encoding: A Practical Guide to Avoiding XSS
item.description: Modern frameworks escape HTML for you in JSX, templates, and components. They don't escape it in URL attributes, inline styles, or anything you build with innerHTML. That's where XSS lives.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Favicon in 2026: Why /favicon.ico Isn't Enough Anymore
item.description: A single 16x16 ICO file used to be enough. Now you need PNG, SVG, multiple sizes, manifest entries, and a dark-mode variant. The good news: it's still ten lines of HTML.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Generating ER Diagrams from SQL Schemas: A 2026 Workflow
item.description: Database design used to start with a hand-drawn ER diagram. In 2026, most teams write SQL first and generate the diagram. Both approaches work. Knowing when to use which is the trick.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Reading DNS Records Like a Sysadmin: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT Explained
item.description: DNS isn't black magic. It's a public lookup table with a dozen record types, each answering a specific question. If you know which question each one answers, you can debug 90% of DNS issues.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: CSV vs JSON: When to Use Which for Data Exchange
item.description: Engineers love JSON. Analysts ask for CSV. Both groups are right, for different reasons. Here's how to pick the format that won't waste anyone's afternoon.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: CSS Gradients Beyond linear-gradient(): Conic, Radial, and Color Spaces
item.description: linear-gradient() is the gradient most teams know about. CSS has three more gradient types and a new color-space system that produces dramatically smoother gradients. Most teams don't use them.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Cron Expressions Decoded: Reading 0 0 * * * Without Cheat Sheets
item.description: Cron is the scheduling syntax that survived 50 years because it's compact and ubiquitous. Once you know the five fields and three special characters, you can read any cron line at a glance.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: CIDR Notation Explained: /24, /16, and the IP Math You Forgot
item.description: CIDR is just IP address ranges in shorthand. /24 means 256 addresses, /16 means 65,536, and the math for everything in between is the same boring power of two.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: BCrypt vs Argon2: Password Hashing in 2026
item.description: Both algorithms are good. The choice in 2026 is less about cryptographic merit and more about library maturity, parameter tuning, and whether you're willing to migrate an existing user base.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: Base64 Demystified: When to Use It, When NOT to Use It
item.description: Stop using Base64 to 'hide' your API keys. It's not encryption. It's not compression. It's a 33% size penalty in exchange for ASCII safety, and that's all it'll ever be.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: AES Encryption Explained for Developers Who Don't Want a PhD in Math
item.description: AES is the symmetric encryption standard. AES-256-GCM is what you should reach for. The math is hard, the usage is short, half a dozen rules and you'll avoid the classic mistakes.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)

item.title: JSON Formatting in 2026: Online vs IDE vs CLI Tools Compared
item.description: Three ways to format JSON in 2026: online formatters, IDE plugins, and CLI tools. Each has trade-offs around privacy, speed, and integration. Here's when to use which.
item.author: noreply@devtoolsonline.dev (DevTools Online Team)
